To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the restitution properties of cardiac electrical conduction and the stability of cardiac spiral waves are determined by the restitution of action potentials and conduction velocities.
the steepness of action potential duration and conduction velocity restitution curves are the major determinants of spiral wave breakup.

the stability of spiral waves in cardiac tissue depends primarily on the restitution properties of the inward currents, and that the most effective strategy to prevent or reverse spiral wave reentry and fibrillation is to alter the restitution of these currents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role that cardiac electrical restitution may play in the initiation and maintenance of cardiac reentrant arrhythmias.
the role of cardiac electrical restitution in the stability and dynamics of spiral wave reentrant arrhythmias.
the role of the restitution properties of the cardiac action potential in the initiation, stability, and termination of reentrant spiral wave arrhythmias.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the APD and CV restitution properties and their interactions with spiral wave dynamics are important factors in the transition from ventricularrhythmic tachycardias to fibrillation.

APD restitution is the main determinant of spiral wave instability in a model of cardiac tissue in which the restitution properties of the ionic currents are eliminated, but that CV restitution is also important and may be more important than APD restitution for promoting spiral wave breakup.
the APD restitution properties of the cardiac action potential are important for the stability of reentrant waves and that the CV restitution properties of the conduction velocity are also important.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the slope of the restitution curve, the width of its range and the restitution of conduction velocity are all important factors for spiral wave breakup.
the stability of spiral waves is determined not only by the APD and CV restitution but also the interaction between them.
the stability of spiral waves is determined by the interplay between APD and CV restitution.
The main takeaway from our work is that

drugs which target ion channels that contribute to the steepness of the APD restitution function may be more useful for treating ventricular tachyarrhythmias than drugs which target ion currents that contribute to APD itself.
a steep slope of APD restitution, and not the absolute value of the maximum slope, is the main determinant of the stability of spiral waves.
the slope of action potential duration restitution is not as important as the range of diatolic intervals over which that slope is steep for promoting spiral breakup.
